metadata.title: Ads in the Picture.
metadata.greeting_note: hello lexicon: Hola (Spanish), one word — fresh for this channel (Kumusta, Sawubona, Hej, Merhaba, Jambo, Vanakkam, Annyeong, Sawadee spent on prior reels). IN-FOR-BEAR LAW in its Yatra form: Bella is the stand-in voice on @Yatra; B00 and the outro say so out loud.
metadata.color_semantics: Fidelity claude palette. ONE terracotta event per beat, and it always marks THE NEW THING ENTERING THE SPACE — the ad tag, the testing stamp, the always-on dot, the seam where ads and agents meet, the open question. Source lines always muted ink.
metadata.note: ILLUSTRATE LAW: Claude UI at B00 (cold open, answered), B03 (ask micro-beat, resolved by B04), B10 verdict, B11 handoff, B12 outro. Every other beat is a purpose-built Adp* scene (ChatAds.tsx). SOURCING (hard, per the human): only the three supplied points, cited 'Jumpfly, October 2026' on screen. The only figure in the reel is 'over 4,000' (apps), rendered verbatim. No ChatGPT/OpenAI UI or logo is imitated — the B04 screen is a generic, labeled redraw.

beats.narration_text: Hello, this is Bella, in for Yatra. ChatGPT is testing ads that appear while you make an image — the same week it gets agents that never switch off.

show.event: Cream page, serif greeting 'Hola, Bella' above the composer — the app greets the narrator; footer chip stays @Yatra
The ask types itself in
Terracotta send arms — the ONE accent
Three result lines stagger in; the third names the marketer question — the ask lands ANSWERED

props.command: OpenAI is testing visual ads during image generation in ChatGPT, and introducing always-on agents the same week. Walk me through both announcements and what they mean for marketers. Cite every claim on screen and add nothing beyond the sources.
output: the ads: a visual format, tested during image generation
the agents: dots — always-on, each with its own cloud computer
the question: is the conversation becoming an ad channel?

beats.narration_text: In one breath: the assistant people use for help, no judgment attached, is making room for advertisers — and learning to work on its own across thousands of apps. That's a question for every marketer.

show.event: Line one rides in from the left on its own rail: 'The helper is getting ads.'
Line two rides in from the right on a second rail: 'The helper is getting agents.'
The two rails bend toward each other and meet at a single terracotta point
At the meeting point the question sets in TERRACOTTA: 'Is the conversation the next ad channel?'
Closer lands beneath

data.slideMeta: The whole story, before any detail
data.meet: Is the conversation the next ad channel?
data.closer: A test today. A question for every marketer.

beats.narration_text: Start with the ads. Per Jumpfly, OpenAI is testing a visual ad format during image generation — rolling out in October to Free and Go plan users in the US, with an initial group of advertisers. A test. But a real one.

show.event: Eyebrow + title set
A TESTING stamp lands top-right in terracotta — the one accent
Six spec rows stamp in, one per spoken fact, each drawing its rule left-to-right: what · where · who · market · when · advertisers
Source line in muted ink: Jumpfly, October 2026

data.title: A new ad format, in testing

beats.narration_text: What does that look like? I asked for the screen, drawn straight from the description.

show.event: Composer returns with the generation prompt already arriving
Terracotta send arms
Running indicator reads 'drawing the screen…' — the result is the next beat

props.command: Draw an image-generation screen the way the announcement describes it: the user's image as the main work, and an ad that is clearly labeled and kept visually separate from it. No brand names, no real ads — the separation is the point.

beats.narration_text: Here it is. Your image is the work. The ad is clearly labeled, and kept visually apart from what you're making. That separation is the promise — near your work, never blended into it.

show.event: A generic generation window draws — no product branding, prompt bar as placeholder lines
The user's image generates top-down inside the main frame: an abstract sun-and-hills composition
A separate panel fades in beside it with a dashed border; its 'Ad' tag sets in TERRACOTTA
A bracket draws across the gap between them: 'visual separation'
Labels set under each: the work / the ad — labeled, kept separate
Redrawn caption + source line in muted ink

beats.narration_text: Why it matters: people bring ChatGPT the question they wouldn't ask a person — a draft, a doubt, a half-formed idea. That's what made it feel judgment-free. Add advertisers, and that space is also an audience. Same space. Different room.

show.event: Three private chat bubbles stack in on the left, one per spoken example
Right side: 'A place to ask.' sets in ink serif
Beneath it, on 'audience', the new line types in TERRACOTTA: 'Also a place to be reached.' — and a faint frame draws around the bubbles
Note: 'Same space. Different room.'

bubbles: a draft I'm not sure about
a question I wouldn't ask out loud

beats.narration_text: Same week, a second announcement. Jumpfly reports OpenAI is introducing dots — always-on AI agents in ChatGPT, each with its own cloud computer, connecting to over four thousand apps through plugins. Not a chatbot waiting. Software that keeps working.

show.event: A single terracotta dot appears and keeps pulsing — always on — labeled 'a dot'
A small cloud-computer box attaches beneath it: 'its own cloud computer'
Lines run out from the dot to a field of app tiles that light up in waves on 'connect'
The figure sets VERBATIM in ink: 'over 4,000' — apps, connected through plugins
Muted 'tiles illustrative' note + source line

beats.narration_text: Put them side by side. One makes ChatGPT a place advertisers pay to appear. The other makes it a place that acts, across your apps, without stopping. Something that can sell, and something that can act — same product, same week.

show.event: Left card sets: ADS — a place advertisers can pay to appear
Right card sets: AGENTS — a place that acts
On 'same product', both cards slide inward until they butt together; the seam between them lights TERRACOTTA: 'the same conversation'
Verdict sets beneath in serif

left.label: a place advertisers can pay to appear

right.label: a place that acts — across apps, always on

data.verdict: Something that can sell. Something that can act.

beats.narration_text: So, marketers: search results became an ad channel. Social feeds did too. Is the AI conversation next? Today it's one format, one moment, a starting group of advertisers. Worth watching from day one.

beats.narration_text: So — the picture. Labeled visual ads, tested in image generation. Always-on agents, reaching over four thousand apps. The judgment-free assistant is becoming two new things at once: a place that acts, and a place that sells.

props.artifactTitle: Ads in the Picture. — the verdict
artifactLines: The ads: a new visual ad format, tested during image generation — rolling out October 2026 to Free and Go plan users in the US, with an initial group of advertisers (Jumpfly, Oct 2026).
The guardrail: the ads are clearly labeled and kept visually separate from the image the user is creating (Jumpfly, Oct 2026).
The agents: dots — always-on AI agents in ChatGPT, each with its own cloud computer, connecting to over 4,000 apps through plugins (Jumpfly, Oct 2026).
The question: an assistant that can act and a surface that can sell — the AI conversation may be the next ad channel. Today it is a test.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Marketers, paste this: I'm a marketer. ChatGPT is testing labeled visual ads during image generation. What would make an ad useful in that moment, what would feel intrusive, and what would I need to know before spending? Then watch whether the answer separates helpful from merely visible.

show.event: Serif 'Your turn.' replaces the persona greeting
The prompt types itself in as the narration reads it aloud, verbatim
Terracotta send arms
Three-item rubric stacks in as the check is discussed
